S88.01.note: The Memory section name in the settings menu was not checked; the link itself is in the code.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Memory section.
Find the link "How memory works" under the memory description.
Click "How memory works".
Check that a help article about memory opens and matches the Memory screen.

labels.text: Search every help article, or browse the help centre by collection.

S88.02.note: The search box placeholder text was not found as a literal in the files read.
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Click "Help center" (it opens in a new tab).
Type a word into the search box on the Help center page and press Enter.
Check that matching articles appear with snippets and links, then click one and check it opens.

S88.03.note: Only the path to the form was checked; the form itself was not traced.
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Look at the support tickets panel at the top of the Help section.
Click "Contact support" (opens in a new tab).
Check that the support page opens where you can describe a problem; check that replies to a ticket appear with a "Send reply" form.

S88.04.note: The exact wording of the bug form fields was not found; diagnostics collection is in apps/web/lib/support/diagnostics/collect.ts.
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Click "Report a bug" (opens in a new tab at the support page, bugs section).
Describe a problem in the bug part of the support page.
Check that the page mentions build and platform details being sent with the report.

S88.05.note: Where the general Feedback button sits was not traced exactly. The plan marks this item as unfinished on mount.
steps: Open a chat.
Click the "Feedback" button near the composer.
Leave the Feedback type on the general option and type a note.
Click "Send feedback" and check that a confirmation appears.
S88.05.where: Feedback > Feedback type > "Send feedback" (in the chat composer)

S88.06.note: Same trigger as S88.05; the plan marks this item as unfinished on mount.
steps: Open a chat.
Click the "Feedback" button near the composer.
Under "Feedback type", choose "Feature request".
Type a request and click "Send feedback"; check that a confirmation appears.
S88.06.where: Feedback > Feedback type > "Feature request" > "Send feedback" (in the chat composer)

S88.07.note: Sharing with support is done through the ticket form in the same panel; the send control was not traced.
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Keep the box "Attach diagnostics: your build, platform and the last few errors this browser recorded." ticked, or untick it.
Click "Review diagnostics" and read the summary in the box labelled "Diagnostics that would be attached".
Click "Download diagnostics" and check the file contents match the summary.

S88.08.needs: a way to make a reply fail
S88.08.note: The reference wording is built by withTurnErrorReference in apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts; its exact visible text was not found as a literal.
steps: Open a chat and send a message in a way that makes the reply fail (for example with the network turned off).
Read the error notice under the reply.
Look for the reference id in the notice text.
Compare it with the reference shown in the message details.
S88.08.where: Chat > a reply that fails > the error notice under the reply

labels.text: Status: hosted dependency and route checks

S88.10.note: The composer footer status feed (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx) has no visible wording that was checked.
steps: Open Settings and go to Help.
Click "System status" (opens the status page in a new tab).
Read the page title "Status: hosted dependency and route checks" and the current status rows.
Compare the rows with what the app shows in the composer footer.

S88.11.needs: an active incident notice (set by the team)
S88.11.note: Notices come from the service notices feed (apps/web/lib/server/service-notices.ts); the visible wording comes from data, not fixed text.
steps: Sign in while an incident notice is active and look at the top of the app.
Check that the notice card shows the problem and its status.
S88.11.where: A notice card near the top of the app while an incident is active

S88.12.needs: a scheduled maintenance notice (set by the team)
S88.12.note: Maintenance notices use a clock icon (apps/web/shared/components/ServiceNotices.tsx); the wording comes from data.
steps: Sign in while a maintenance notice is scheduled and look at the top of the app.
Check that the maintenance notice shows the planned time.
S88.12.where: A notice card in the app before and during planned maintenance

S88.13.needs: a new release in the release feed
S88.13.note: The banner shows only when a release has not been seen in this browser.
steps: Sign in after a new release is published, or clear the saved last-seen release value in the browser to test again.
Read the banner "What's new:" followed by the headline.
Click the banner link and check it opens the release notes for that release.
Click the dismiss control and check the banner goes away.
S88.13.where: A banner at the top of the app that starts with "What's new:" after an update

S88.14.needs: a model marked as retiring or retired in the catalogue
S88.14.note: The model picker row wording is built from data ("Leaving" plus the model short name), so it depends on the catalogue state.
steps: Open a chat that uses a model marked as retiring.
Look at the model picker in the composer footer for the row that reads "Leaving" the model name.
Look at the notice that says the model "is no longer available" and says which model replaces it.
Click the dismiss control on the notice and check it closes.
S88.14.where: Composer footer > model picker: a row that reads "Leaving" a model, or a notice that says "is no longer available"

S88.15.note: The button that opens the import dialog was not found as a literal; the dialog itself is in apps/web/features/settings/components/ImportMemoryDialog.tsx.
steps: Open Settings and go to Memory.
Open the memory import dialog.
Choose a source such as "ChatGPT", then choose a .txt or .json file.
Check the preview step lists what will be imported before you confirm the import.
S88.15.where: Settings > Memory > import dialog (choose a source, pick a file, then preview)

S88.16.note: The link text on the Privacy page was not found; the request form was not traced.
steps: Open Settings and go to Privacy.
Find the link to rights requests and click it.
On the "Exercise your rights." page, read the "Your requests" list if you have any.
Check each listed request shows its reference, type (Access, Correction or Erasure) and status.
S88.16.where: Settings > Privacy > rights-request link > "Exercise your rights." page

S88.17.note: The save button's visible text was not found; network-level enforcement is not checked here.
steps: Open "Cookie preferences" from the cookies page or the cookie banner.
Turn analytics off and keep necessary cookies on, then save.
Reload the page and open "Cookie preferences" again.
Check analytics is still off and necessary is still locked on, and no banner returns.
S88.17.where: "Cookie preferences" (cookie preference centre, opened from the cookies page or the cookie banner)

S88.18.note: The success text is in the same file as the code, around line 1189.
steps: Open a chat with a reply.
Find "Report this response" on the reply.
Click it and check the message "Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it." appears.
Check the report button shows it was sent and cannot be sent again.
S88.18.where: Under a chat reply: "Report this response"

S88.19.needs: none (a link to the form was not found in the app)
S88.19.note: No in-app link to the copyright form was found; the form is reached by its address only.
steps: Open /copyright/report in a browser.
Read the legend "What you are reporting" and choose the type of report.
Fill in the reporter fields and submit.
Check the result shows "recorded" with a reference number.

S88.20.needs: a refused reply (needs a safety refusal from the provider)
S88.20.note: The refusal notice text was not found as a literal; it is shown from ChatMessageList.tsx when a refusal finishes.
steps: Get a chat reply that the provider refuses for safety reasons.
Find the notice under the refused reply and click "Report issue".
Describe the refusal and click "Submit report".
Check a confirmation appears.
S88.20.where: Under a refused chat reply: "Report issue" > "Submit report"

labels.text: Why should the suspension be lifted?

S88.21.needs: a suspended account (or the appeal page)
S88.21.note: Only the appeal path was traced; the suspension reason text is not a fixed literal.
steps: Sign in to a suspended account, or open the appeal page at /appeal.
Read the account access notice that explains the suspension.
Type a reason under "Why should the suspension be lifted?" and click "Submit appeal".
Check the appeal thread shows your appeal and the note "A person reviews every appeal."
S88.21.where: Sign-in screen for a suspended account: "Submit appeal" (or "Why should the suspension be lifted?")

S88.22.note: The security.txt route is in apps/web/app/.well-known/security.txt/route.ts; no in-app link was checked.
steps: Open /security in a browser.
Scroll to the section "Reporting a vulnerability.".
Read the reporting instructions and the contact the page names.
Check /.well-known/security.txt also opens and lists a contact.

S88.23.note: No in-app link to the accessibility page was found; the support panel has accessibility text at SupportTicketsPanel.tsx line 583 that was not traced.
steps: Open /accessibility in a browser.
Scroll to the section "Report a barrier.".
Read how to report an accessibility barrier and the channel it names.
Check the channel can be used without a mouse (keyboard and screen reader).
Open Settings and go to Help.
Click "Legal" (it opens the legal page in a new tab).
Open a policy and find the "Previous versions" link under its date.
Click it and check earlier dated versions of the policy and what changed are listed.

S88.25.note: No in-app link to the subprocessors page was found in the Help section.
steps: Open /subprocessors in a browser.
Read the page title "Subprocessors." and the "Last updated:" line.
Read the list of subprocessors.
Check the change log link (to /changelog) is present.

labels.text: Claims with dates, and the ones we cannot make.

S88.26.note: Partial: the plan says the owner has not yet commissioned SOC 2, ISO 27001 or a penetration test, so there are no reports to review. No in-app link to /trust was found.
steps: Open /trust in a browser.
Read the heading and the section "Audit reports".
Read the "SOC 2" and "ISO 27001" rows, which say no report is held.
Compare with Expected: the page states no reports or certificates are published yet.
S88.26.where: Browser address bar: /trust (heading "Claims with dates, and the ones we cannot make.")

S88.27.note: Expected says notices appear automatically for users in a jurisdiction; the code has no location check. The India and EU pages are fixed pages reached by link, and the plan's Where line 'not written yet' is out of date. I did not trace the route from the first screen into Settings, and I found no region-block notice in the code.
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and choose the Help tab.
Click the Legal item (it opens the /legal page).
Find and click the India: DPDP notice link. Check that the page titled Notice to Data Principals in India. loads and shows the DPDP Act, 2023 notice.

Go back to Legal and click EU representative. Check that the page says no representative is currently appointed under Article 27 GDPR, with the date-stamped status text and where to send privacy requests.
S88.27.where: Settings > Help > Legal > India: DPDP notice (the EU representative page is reached the same way through the Legal page, or from the footer Legal list)
